title: Lab 203 - Linux Basic Commands & Navigation

lab_objective.description: By the end of this lab, you will be able to perform basic Linux commands, navigate the Linux filesystem, create files and directories, move and copy files, create nested directory structures, and collect and document basic server information.
lab_objective.scenario: You are working as a Linux System Administrator and have been asked to perform a basic server assessment and filesystem management exercise. While working from your home directory, you must collect important server information, create and organize files and directories, navigate the filesystem, and document the required command outputs for review.
prerequisites: SSH access to the Linux server
Basic understanding of Linux command-line interface
objectives: Understand and use basic Linux commands.
Display and verify the current working directory.
Check and display the Linux kernel version.
Display hidden files and their detailed information.
Create files and directories using Linux commands.
Move and copy files between directories.
Create nested directory structures using mkdir.
Use the tree command to display directory structures.
Redirect and append command output to files.
Document basic server information for review.

tasks.title: Display Current Working Directory
steps: While you are in your home directory, display your current working directory.
Append the output of the command to a file named server_info located in your home directory.
Do not overwrite existing content in server_info.

tasks.title: Check Kernel Version
steps: Check and display the kernel version of the server.
Append the output of the command to the server_info file.
Do not overwrite existing content in server_info.

tasks.title: Display Detailed File Listing
steps: Display a detailed listing of the files in the current directory.
The output should include permissions, ownership, and file size.
Append the output of the command to the server_info file.
Do not overwrite existing content in server_info.

tasks.title: Display Hidden Files
steps: List all files, including hidden files, with detailed information.
Append the output of the command to the server_info file.
Do not overwrite existing content in server_info.

tasks.title: Create and Navigate to Linux Directory
steps: Create a directory named Linux.
Navigate into the 'Linux' directory.

tasks.title: Verify Linux Directory
steps: While you are inside 'Linux' Directory Verify that you are inside the Linux directory.
Display the present working directory and redirect the output to '~/server_info'.

tasks.title: Create Linux Subdirectories
steps: Inside the Linux directory, create the following subdirectories:
Redhat
oel
debian

tasks.title: Return to Home Directory
steps: Move back to your home directory using cd...
Verify your current working directory.
Append the output of the command to the server_info file.
Do not overwrite existing content in server_info.

tasks.title: Create Empty Files
steps: While in your home directory, create the following empty files:
file1.txt
pic.jpg
clip.avi

tasks.title: Create Directories and Organize Files
steps: Create the following directories in your home directory:
documents
images
media
Move file1.txt to the documents directory.
Move pic.jpg to the images directory.
Move clip.avi to the media directory.

tasks.title: Create Nested Directory Structure
steps: Using a single mkdir command with the appropriate option, create the following nested directory structure:
office/hobby/personal

tasks.title: Copy file1.txt
steps: Copy file1.txt from the documents directory to the office directory.

tasks.title: Copy pic.jpg
steps: Copy pic.jpg from the images directory to the office/hobby directory.

tasks.title: Display and Save Office Directory Structure
steps: Display the directory structure of the office directory using the tree command.
Save the output in a file named office_tree.
The office_tree file must be located in office/hobby/personal/.

completion_message: Cool!!!! Great Job. You have successfully completed Linux Basic Commands & Navigation Lab.
